comparator.name: Law: Business Law specialisation (Rechtsgeleerdheid: Ondernemingsrecht)
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg’s current official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS. Year 1 is the common 60-ECTS Law foundation. Year 2 is a compulsory 60-ECTS sequence combining EU and public-law foundations with property, contract, liability, international law, philosophy, law and economics, and Business Law. Year 3 is a compulsory 60-ECTS Business Law specialisation in organisation and strategy, corporate finance, business ethics, criminal liability, taxation, procedure, labour law, moot court and an 8-ECTS thesis. Zero-credit Dutch-language testing, mentoring and the Tilburg Skills Lab are programme features but are excluded from the credit total. The programme page mentions that study abroad may be possible, but its published 2026–27 table specifies 60 compulsory ECTS in year 3, so no unallocated exchange space is invented.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target explicitly names Tilburg’s Business Law specialisation within the Law bachelor. The current official 2026–27 curriculum page confirms this exact route and supplies its complete three-year curriculum.

core: Company and business law, corporate structure, governance, shareholder relations and directors’ responsibilities
Private law, property, contracts and liability
Constitutional, criminal, administrative, European and international legal foundations
Legal practice, procedure, advocacy, research and the Business Law thesis
Corporate finance, law and economics, taxation and valuation
Organisation, strategy, business ethics and legal responsibility
European legal history and philosophy of law
adjacent: Corporate responsibility, sustainability and environmental liability
Innovative companies, entrepreneurship and legal form
questions: How should law govern mergers, shareholder disputes, directors’ liability and strategic corporate decisions?

alternatives.label: Business law, governance & corporate finance
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines UCR’s full available law sequence with transnational business law, accounting and corporate finance, economics, international business governance, organisational psychology, negotiation, leadership communication and entrepreneurship.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Tilburg’s Business Law specialisation: a legal core in private, criminal, constitutional, European and international law combined with company law, corporate finance, economics, governance, organisation, negotiation and applied business research.
progression: Law and business gateways, economics, methods and communication foundations precede private, criminal, international, business-law, finance, governance and advanced organisational work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Business law, corporate responsibility & sustainability
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains the UCR law and business-law core but reorganises the remaining study around climate change, environmental governance, sustainability research, responsible organisations, environmental communication and data literacy.
alternatives.concept: A distinct corporate-responsibility route grounded in Tilburg’s explicit business-ethics, sustainability and environmental-liability interests, combining law and transnational business law with sustainability science, environmental governance, climate communication and social responsibility.
progression: Law, business and sustainability gateways precede advanced private, criminal, international, constitutional, EU and transnational business law together with advanced sustainability and environmental-governance work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: This route differs from the closest programme by eleven courses each way (82.5 ECTS). It replaces corporate finance, entrepreneurship, organisational psychology, negotiation and market-research breadth with climate, sustainability, environmental governance, environmental communication, social movements and data study, making corporate responsibility rather than general business-law practice its organising priority.

candidates.label: Corporate responsibility, sustainability and environmental liability
Innovative-company legal strategy
candidates.rationale: The innovative-company interest is coherent but already implemented by the closest route’s entrepreneurship, product-design, strategy, finance, company-law and governance courses. It does not support a third materially different 24-course legal curriculum without adding unrelated technology courses merely to cross the distinctness threshold.

selection.assessment: The closest route owns the Business Law core, corporate-governance, finance, strategy and professional-practice interests. Corporate responsibility and sustainability form one evidence-backed, feasible and materially distinct second route. Innovative-company legal strategy was assessed separately, but its only generator row is already substantively implemented by the closest route and does not justify a third distinct law curriculum. Production therefore stops at two alternatives.

blocks: Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no dedicated European legal-history course.
Explicitly unmatched: Principles of Private Law is already aligned to the more advanced property-law component and cannot represent both components.
Explicitly unmatched: Foundations of European Union Law is already aligned to the advanced EU-law component.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no dedicated Dutch administrative-law course.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no dedicated tax-law course.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no second dedicated advanced contract-law course.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no dedicated administrative legal-protection course.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR Ethics is general rather than a dedicated philosophy-of-law course.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no dedicated civil-liability-law course.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR’s single criminal-law course is already aligned to the introductory criminal-law component.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no dedicated criminal-procedure course.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no dedicated civil-procedure and dispute-resolution course.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no dedicated labour-law course.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations provides the organisational and venture context for introductory company law without replacing its legal doctrine.
Introduction to Economics supplies the economic foundations used in law-and-economics analysis, while Tilburg applies them specifically to business law.
Accounting & Corporate Finance directly develops financial-statement and corporate-finance analysis relevant to business valuation and financing.
Transnational Business Law directly covers company law, contracts, trade, intellectual property and commercial disputes.
International Business & Governance examines organisational strategy, corporate responsibility and governance in an international institutional context.
Negotiation & Strategic Thinking develops structured argument, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills, but does not reproduce a company-law moot court.
Explicitly unmatched: UCR has economics and public-finance study but no dedicated taxation-of-enterprise law course.
Ethics develops normative analysis of responsibility and conflicting obligations; Tilburg applies that reasoning specifically to corporate conduct.
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops structured written and oral argument relevant to procedural-law practice, but is not a legal-skills practicum.
The comparator requires an 8-ECTS independent Business Law thesis. No scheduled UCR course is presented as an equivalent thesis; the standard Optional independent research element is aligned here.

notes.text: Tilburg’s specialisation is a Dutch-law degree with continuous company-law doctrine, civil and criminal procedure, tax and labour law, a company-law moot court and a Business Law thesis. UCR can combine its available law courses with business, finance, governance, negotiation and sustainability, but these are related interdisciplinary pathways rather than a qualifying Dutch Business Law curriculum.

UCR does not reproduce Tilburg’s dedicated sequences in Dutch administrative law, tax law, liability law, labour law, civil and criminal procedure, legal philosophy, company-law moot court or the integrated Skills Lab. Those gaps remain explicit rather than being filled with weak substitutes.

The Tilburg specialisation is Dutch-taught and includes a compulsory zero-credit Dutch-language test; UCR is English-taught. The comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language eligibility.
